items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: I ain't got a (?)quarter to one(?)." So as I said, I left and I went uptown and found out that Minton was out of town, so I played them two weeks and I saved me twenty-five dollars a week, and I come down there the next and put my fifty dollars down.

ctx.x: ...but he could play the piano. And he could write. But he didn't know how to write for saxophone. Man, he'd write some parts up there where your fingers would be twisting. He could play that on piano, but some things you don't write for saxophone players to play way up high. But I scuffled and played them.

And he got this job at a little club up on Seventh Avenue... I found out that the union man, Minton, had gone on vacation, and he'd be gone for two weeks. So that meant there wasn't nobody who'd be checking the places up in Harlem. So I went down to the union to put in my transfer, and the man said, "You can't put in no transfer." He went out and checked my records (and I left my transfer), and he said, "You got to join!" I said, "Join? I ain't got a (?)quarter to one(?)." So as I said, I left and I went uptown…
